sentences.text: The second key part of Rule nineteen applies unless you’ve already determined that no risk of collision exists.

Every vessel that hears, apparently forward of her beam, the fog signal of another vessel, or that cannot avoid a close-quarters situation with another vessel forward of her beam, shall reduce her speed to the minimum at which she can be kept on her course.
She shall, if necessary, take all her way off, and in any event navigate with extreme caution until the danger of collision is over.
Sound travels unpredictably in fog, so you can’t fully trust the direction a signal seems to come from.
